newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LATE BRITISH SCRIBE DOBEREINER HONORED BY U.S. GOLF WRITERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LATE BRITISH SCRIBE DOBEREINER HONORED BY U.S. GOLF WRITERS.

text.p: The late British writer Peter Dobereiner was named winner of the Golf Writers Association of America's William H. Richardson Award for his consistent contribution to golf.
Dobereiner, who died of cancer last summer, travelled worldwide to cover the sport, writing nearly 30 books on the game, its players and its courses.
He served as golf correspondent for The Guardian and The Observer in Britain and entertained readers of Golf Digest magazine for nearly 20 years with wit and style.
Dobereiner received 110 votes to 83 for CBS Television producer-director Frank Chirkinian, known for his pioneering coverage of The Masters, and 42 for former LPGA commissioner Charles Mechem.
U.S. Open champion Steve Jones was named winner of the GWAA's Ben Hogan Award, given to a player making a comeback from significant injury.
Jones suffered ligament and joint damage to his left ring finger in a dirt bike accident in November 1991. While seemingly not a major injury, it affected a major part of the golf swing -- the grip.
Jones missed the entire 1992 and 1993 seasons, finally developed a reverse grip and returned to the tour. His comeback climaxed with victory at the 1996 U.S. Open at Oakland Hills Country Club.
